verdicts.a_text_starts: Unprocessed red meat consumption is not associated with incident stroke.
verdicts.b_text_starts: Consumption of 100 g/day of unprocessed red meat is associated with an 11% increased risk
verdicts.reason: Both are meta-analyses of unprocessed red meat and incident stroke on comparable adult populations; a 2010 pooled null vs a 2016 updated point estimate — the canonical time-updated red-meat disagreement.

verdicts.a_text_starts: The decreased risk of myocardial infarction was similar between men consuming less than 10
verdicts.b_text_starts: Increased alcohol consumption is log-linearly associated with a lower risk of myocardial infarction
verdicts.reason: Different populations (US male health professionals only vs mixed IPD across 19 countries) AND different dose constructs (per-drinking-day vs per-week). The apparent conflict evaporates once the measures are reconciled — a regime-conflation, not a real disagreement.

verdicts.a_text_starts: Alcohol consumption is not significantly associated with overall incident stroke compared
verdicts.b_text_starts: Higher alcohol consumption is roughly linearly associated with a higher risk of stroke
verdicts.reason: Both are meta-analyses of adult drinkers with comparable methods; an older pooled null vs a newer IPD's linear positive slope. Direct disagreement on whether an aggregate association exists.
verdicts.topic: alcohol / stroke — is there an association?

verdicts.a_text_starts: Alcohol consumption exhibits a curvilinear J-shaped dose-response relationship
verdicts.b_text_starts: Higher alcohol consumption is roughly linearly associated with a higher risk of stroke
verdicts.reason: Both meta-analyses on comparable populations; the disagreement is model choice (fractional-polynomial J-shape vs assumed linear). A modelling-choice disagreement on the same construct is a substantive disagreement.

verdicts.a_text_starts: Unprocessed red meat intake is not associated with incident diabetes mellitus.
verdicts.b_text_starts: Higher intake of red meat is associated with increased incidence of type 2 diabetes.
verdicts.reason: Same time-updated red-meat pattern as pair #1: 2010 pooled null vs 2019 umbrella-positive on the same construct.

verdicts.a_text_starts: Alcohol consumption is associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality
verdicts.b_text_starts: Analyses of higher-quality, bias-free studies fail to find a reduced mortality risk
verdicts.reason: Same construct (light drinking vs abstention on all-cause mortality) but with Stockwell's abstainer-bias correction applied. The central controversy in alcohol epidemiology; systematic reviews reaching opposite conclusions after quality adjustment.
verdicts.topic: alcohol / all-cause mortality — J-shape vs quality-adjusted null
